q: I'm over 50. Can I still start?
a: Yes. Start from Day 1: today. People 50 and older can save extra in 401(k)s and IRAs each year. Paying off debt and timing Social Security also make a real difference. See the 50+ tab on Your path.

q: My pay changes every week. Can I still save?
a: Yes. Pick a tiny amount you can save even in a slow week, like $5, and add more in good weeks. Build your cushion first, and set aside money for taxes from each payment.

q: Should I pay off debt or invest first?
a: Debt over 15% APR, like most credit cards, usually grows faster than investments do. Paying it off first is like earning a sure return. If your job matches 401(k) savings, getting that match usually still makes sense.
If an FDIC-insured bank closes, the U.S. government protects your money, up to $250,000 per person. Credit unions have the same kind of protection from the NCUA.

q: I don't have a bank account. Where do I start?
a: Look for a bank or credit union with no monthly fee and no minimum balance. Many accept a passport, consular ID or ITIN. The Getting banked tab on Your path walks through the steps.

q: How do I know if a broker or adviser is safe?
a: Look them up for free on FINRA BrokerCheck before you give them any money. Ask how they are paid. Be careful with anyone who promises big, sure returns.

q: What if I need to pause my plan?
a: That's normal. Life happens. Keep your emergency cushion, stop adding for a while, and pick up again when you can. Pausing is part of the plan.
